newsitem.title: UK: Merrill Lynch says no decision made on new office.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch says no decision made on new office.

text.p: Merrill Lynch, the U.S. investment bank, said on Sunday it had not finalised any decision on where to build its new London headquarters.
The bank could not confirm a report in Britain's Sunday Telegraph newspaper which said Merrill is set to move to an old Post Office site in London's City.
"No decision has been made. We continue to explore all our options," said Rich Silverman, manager of media relations at Merrill Lynch in London.
The Telegraph report, quoting insiders from the bank, said Merrill was in "advanced negotiations" on plans to spend 160 million pounds to buy the 500,000 square foot City site and build headquarters.
It said Merrill's decision was expected to be ratified by the bank's board in New York in the next few weeks.

A press officer from the Corporation of London -- the local authority for London's financial centre -- said a number of possibilities had been looked at by Merrill Lynch, but could not confirm that any decision had been made.
She said more information would be avaiable after a planning meeting on March 25.
